chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Darraj said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') who shaved his head in Mecca. He said: 'If he was ignorant, there is no penalty upon him. And if he deliberately did that in the first thirty days of the months for Hajj, there is no penalty upon him. And if he deliberately did that after the thirty days in which the hair is allowed to grow for Hajj, then upon him is a blood offering (dam) which he must pour out.'

key_terms.أَوَّلِ الشُّهُورِ: The beginning of the months (of Hajj)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: One performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يُوفَّرُ فِيهَا الشَّعْرُ: In which the hair is allowed to grow

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for shaving the head early during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the penalty for premature shaving in Hajj al-Tamattu', distinguishing between ignorance and deliberate intent, as well as the timing relative to the thirty-day hair growth period. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on *dam* (blood offering, typically a sheep) as a compensatory sacrifice for violating the ritual sequence, underscoring the balance between strict adherence to ritual order and leniency for the unaware.
